WITH gender_counts AS (
  SELECT c.gender, COUNT(*) AS invoice_count
  FROM Invoices AS i
  JOIN Orders AS o ON o.order_id = i.order_id
  JOIN Customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
  GROUP BY c.gender
), overall_average AS (
  SELECT AVG(invoice_count) AS avg_invoice_count
  FROM gender_counts
), above_average AS (
  SELECT gc.invoice_count, oa.avg_invoice_count
  FROM gender_counts AS gc
  CROSS JOIN overall_average AS oa
  WHERE gc.invoice_count > oa.avg_invoice_count
)
SELECT AVG(avg_invoice_count) AS overall_average_invoice_count,
       AVG(invoice_count - avg_invoice_count) AS average_excess_over_overall_average
FROM above_average

assumptions.assumption: “Invoiced activity” means the number of invoice records per customer gender; each invoice is counted once.
